strings.name: Nikesh Arora
strings.role: Technology executive · Palo Alto Networks chairman and CEO
strings.summary: Trained in electrical engineering, management and finance, Arora moved from investment and telecommunications into internet business. He led regional and global commercial operations at Google, then held leadership roles at SoftBank. Since 2018 he has led Palo Alto Networks, integrating network, cloud and security operations. Its 2026 CyberArk and Chronosphere acquisitions extended identity security and observability.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through 16 November 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: His work across Google's global business, SoftBank investment and Palo Alto Networks connects the platform economy with cybersecurity.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.f2.label: Education
strings.facts.f2.value: Electrical engineering degree at IT-BHU; graduate management and finance studies at Northeastern and Boston College.
strings.highlights.h1.title: From platform business to security
strings.highlights.h1.text: He brought commercial experience from Google and SoftBank into enterprise cybersecurity.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Integrating security products
strings.highlights.h2.text: At Palo Alto Networks, he pursued platforms through acquisitions and internal development.
strings.timeline.t1.title: CyberArk acquisition completed
strings.timeline.t1.text: The company added identity and privileged-access technology; product integration remained further work.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Chronosphere acquisition completed
strings.timeline.t2.text: The company expanded into observability across application, infrastructure and security data.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Leading Palo Alto Networks
strings.timeline.t3.text: He became CEO and chairman, succeeding Mark McLaughlin.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Leaving SoftBank leadership
strings.timeline.t4.text: He stepped down as representative director and director after the shareholder meeting, then moved to an advisory role.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Joining SoftBank
strings.timeline.t5.text: He moved from Google to vice chairman and US business leadership, later becoming president and COO.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Joining Google
strings.timeline.t6.text: He entered its European business and later led regional and global sales, development and commercial operations.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Starting in investments
strings.timeline.t7.text: At Fidelity he began finance and technology-management work before moving into telecoms and the internet.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Engineering degree
strings.timeline.t8.text: He completed electrical engineering at IT-BHU before further studies in the United States.
